learning_outcomes.text: Knows the fundamental notions of professional ethics, the differences between ethics, morality, deontology, integrity.
Understands the principles and legal standards regarding good conduct in research, development, innovation activities (Law 206/2004).
Has knowledge about preventing and combating plagiarism, about the ethics of drafting scientific papers, and about academic responsibility.
Understands the relevant provisions of the Labor Code and the Codes of Ethics and Professional Deontology in academia and industry.
Knows the essential concepts regarding corruption, transparency, conflict of interest, and whistleblowers.
Uses digital tools for presenting specialized papers.
Plans the stages of drafting a report on a topic related to the course theme.
Operates with concepts specific to this discipline.

Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the work group and applies effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, across various hierarchical levels.
Constantly informs and documents himself/herself in his/her field of activity by adequately using effective lifelong learning methods and techniques.

syllabus_topics: General notions of ethics and integrity. Objectives, methods, definitions, interdisciplinary approaches. Connection with morality

Traditions in ethics and integrity, theoretical ethics related to applied ethics, vulnerabilities, consequences, probabilities of manifestation and risks in activity. Consequences of violating ethical principles
About plagiarism. Definitions, history, famous examples, similarity
Provisions of Law no. 206/2004 regarding good conduct in scientific research
Harassment and inappropriate behavior in the collective
Methodology for developing codes of ethics and integrity
Provisions of the code of ethics and professional deontology of UT Iasi
Conceiving, structuring, and drafting a bachelor's thesis. Ethics and plagiarism issues
Legislation in the field of ethics
Analysis of the Ethics Committee report
teaching_methods: Debates based on Power Point presentations
Discovery learning models facilitated by direct and indirect exploration of reality

assessment_methods.method: Systematic observation of students (individual/team assignments, report preparation - case study) (part of Examen/Colocviu)
Formative evaluation test (checks during the semester) (part of Examen/Colocviu)
Summative evaluation test (final check) (part of Examen/Colocviu)
Active participation in activities and evaluation test (seminar)

assessment_rules: The student passes the Ethics and Integrity discipline if they demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the fundamental principles of professional and academic ethics, the ability to identify and apply moral conduct and integrity norms in academic and professional activity, as well as assuming responsible, honest, and respectful behavior towards the values of the institution and society. The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits.
